newsitem.title: GREECE: SARANDOPOULOS ISSUES 2.5 BLN CONVERTIBLE BOND.
newsitem.headline: SARANDOPOULOS ISSUES 2.5 BLN CONVERTIBLE BOND.

text.p: Construction firm K.I.Sarandopoulos expects 1996 turnover of 9.1 billion drachmas, up 2.25 percent on 1995 but earnings will be flat around 1.8 billion, company executives told reporters.

The company got the Athens stock exchange's approval for a 2.52 billion drachma convertible bond issue and will use proceeds to finance its participation in the Rio-Antirio bridge and Elefsis-Stavros-Spata highway project.

It will issue 1,445,310 five-year convertible bonds with a fixed 9.0 percent coupon which will be listed on the Athens bourse. The minimum trading lot will be 10 bonds. Societe Generale is acting as agent for the issue.
The bonds will be available to shareholders of record on December 3 at 1,750 drachmas per bond. Rights will entitle shareholders to 10 convertibles for every 40 shares held.
The subscription period for the convertibles ends January 9 1997 and the issue date will be January 13. The bonds will have a par value of 900 drachmas.

Each bond may be converted to one share at 2,100 drachmas at any time during the five year maturity. Shareholders who opt for conversion into shares will have to pay 350 drachmas to the company -- the difference between the conversion price and the issue price.
The minimum conversion lot will also be 10 bonds.

The convertibles are callable one year after the issue date if the shares exceed a market price of 3,000 drachmas on the Athens bourse. Bondholders will also get any accrued interest if their bonds are called away, company executives said.
Still, bondholders may still opt for conversion if the bonds are called away, the company's chief financial officer said.
Corporate convertible bonds are subject to a tax rate of 20 percent. Thus the net yield on the bonds will be 7.2 percent.
"The Sarandopoulos family as majority shareholders with a 70 percent stake will exercise their rights and subscribe to the bond issue," chairman Costantine Sarandopoulos said.
With a present orderbook of uncompleted projects amounting to 49 billion drachmas, Sarandopoulos has stakes in the consortia that will build key infrastructure projects.
It has a 5.0 percent stake in the Gefyra joint venture which will build the Rio-Antirio bridge budgeted at 225 billion drachmas.
Sarandopoulos is among the five contractors carrying out earth moving works for Hochtief which is constructing the new Athens international airport at Spata.
It also participates in Attiki Odos with a 6.2 percent stake on the Elefsis-Stavros-Spata highway which will link Athens with its new airport.
The company also undertook the refurbishment of Tirana airport in Albania, a project budgeted at 2.5 billion drachmas, executives said.
